the biosolid containing biogenic sulphide precipitates and spent WAC can be considered as a safe disposal option.
the biogenic sulphides and iron sulphide formed in AGR were stable and the biosolids formed were non-toxic and safe to dispose.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biosolid formed in the AGR is stable under all conditions tested and can be considered as a potential candidate for safe arsenic and iron removal from groundwater.
biogenic arsenosulfide-iron sulfide precipitates can be used as an arsenic removal material for the treatment of contaminated water.
the biosolid containing biogenic arsenosulfides and iron sulphide are stable under oxic and anoxic conditions and are unlikely to release arsenic to the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosolides containing arsenosulphide and iron sulphide are stable under all the conditions tested and hence can be safely applied to the field.
the biosolid formed in the AGR is a safe and stable solid waste that can be used for land application without further treatment.
the biogenic arsenosulfide and iron sulfide precipitates formed under anoxic conditions are stable and can be used for arsenic removal from aqueous phase.
